question: 1. Eligibility to open online
rule: Must be 18 or older; needs government-issued photo ID (driver's license, passport, etc.), proof of address, and SSN or ITIN. The Deposit Account Agreement (DAA) says Chase may require name, residential address, date of birth and SSN, driver's license or other identifying documents, and may restrict or close the account if it can't get the information its Know Your Customer rules need.
citation: Chase, 'Opening a Checking Account Online' education page; Chase Deposit Account Agreement eff. 6/14/2026, Sec. IX (identification)
jurisdiction: US (federal: 31 CFR 1020.220); account located in the applicant's state if Chase has a branch there, otherwise Ohio law
uncertainty: Low on age, ID and SSN/ITIN. ChexSystems/Early Warning: no official Chase statement found. The DAA only covers verification in general terms. Chase co-owns Early Warning Services, and third-party sources say Chase screens with EWS, but that is not confirmed by an official source.
gameImplication: A US citizen aged 18+ with an SSN and a New Haven address passes the eligibility gate. Model a small chance of a screening decline only if the game tracks a prior-bank-abuse history.

question: 2. Channels / New Haven branch
rule: Can be opened online, in the Chase Mobile app or in a branch. Chase has a branch at 234 Church St, New Haven CT 06510.

uncertainty: Medium on the branch. The official Chase locator page (chase.com/locator) would not render, so the address comes from third-party directories.
gameImplication: The player can open online or walk into a branch downtown.

question: 3. Approval timing / identity failure

gameImplication: Model as usually instant, with a small chance of a 'visit a branch with ID' detour. Label this as a game assumption, not a sourced figure.

question: 4. Minimum opening deposit / funding deadline / funding methods
rule: No minimum opening deposit is stated for Total Checking. The monthly fee is $15, or $0 with $500+ in qualifying electronic deposits, a $1,500 daily balance, a $5,000 average balance or a linked account. Funding methods listed: direct deposit, transfers from other banks, QuickDeposit mobile check deposit, Zelle, branch or ATM. No funding deadline found. The DAA says Chase 'may automatically close your account if the balance is $0 or negative.'

uncertainty: Medium: no specific unfunded-account deadline was published, only the discretionary $0-balance closure.
gameImplication: Opening deposit is $0. An unfunded or $0 account can be closed by Chase at its discretion, with no fixed day count.

uncertainty: Low on about a week. A search snippet said 3-5 days on another Chase page, which conflicts. Digital card not found.

question: 6. Funds availability and external transfers

Special new-account rules for the first 30 days apply to checks only (up to the 7th business day). The maximum daily limit applicable to you will be displayed at the time you set up the transfer.'

question: 7. Closing the account
rule: DAA: 'Either you or we may close your account at any time ... We are not required to close your account at your request if you have pending transactions, the account is overdrawn, your account is subject to legal process ... or any type of holds.' Chase may return the balance (less fees) if greater than $1. Chase help content says the account must be at a zero balance, then close by phone or secure message. The 6/14/2026 DAA has no early-closure fee: a text search for 'early' found only CD early-withdrawal penalties. Recurring payments are not stated to be auto-cancelled. Statement access after closing: not found in the DAA.
citation: Chase DAA eff. 6/14/2026, Sec. VIII 'Closing Your Account'
uncertainty: Medium. The '$25 fee if closed within 90 days' claim on third-party sites is NOT in the current DAA. The 90-day rule that does exist is a bonus-eligibility rule: no new-account bonus if a Chase account was closed within 90 days. The zero-balance-first and secure-message details come from a search snippet, not a fetched page.
gameImplication: No early-closure fee. The player must clear pending items and avoid a negative balance. Closing by secure message or phone is effectively online.

question: 8b. Is there a US equivalent of the UK CASS?
rule: No national, mandated account-switching service exists in the US. CFPB consumer guidance (updated June 4, 2025) tells consumers to do every step themselves: list automatic payments and deposits, change direct deposit, leave money in the old account until items clear, transfer funds, close, and 'Ask for written confirmation when the old account is closed.' The CFPB 1033 Personal Financial Data Rights rule (final Oct 2024) concerns data portability, not switching. In 2026 it is enjoined by a federal court (E.D. Ky.) and under CFPB reconsideration, with compliance dates stayed. Bank tools are limited to forms and, at BofA, a payroll-login direct-deposit switch.
citation: CFPB 'Moving your checking account'; Federal Register 2025-16139 (1033 reconsideration); law-firm alerts
uncertainty: Low on 'no CASS equivalent'. Medium on 1033's exact litigation status (secondary sources).
gameImplication: A US switch is a manual multi-step chore. The game should not move payments for the player.

question: 9a. Next-business-day availability for electronic payments

(b)(2): received when the bank has '(i) Payment in actually and finally collected funds; and (ii) Information on the account and amount to be credited.'

question: 9b. New-account exception
rule: 12 CFR 229.13(a): 'An account is considered a new account during the first 30 calendar days after the account is established.' Cash and electronic payments must still follow 229.10(a) and (b) (next business day). Checks are covered only up to the first $6,725 per banking day, with the excess available by the 9th business day; local and nonlocal check schedules do not apply.

question: 1b. Federal identity requirements
rule: 31 CFR 1020.220(a)(2): banks must obtain name, date of birth, address and an identification number (a TIN for US persons) before opening an account. They verify by documents, non-documentary methods (for example, consumer reporting databases), or both. The CIP must address when the bank will not open an account, when a customer may use an account while verification is pending, and when to close an account after failed verification. Records are kept for 5 years after closure.

question: 11. Article 10 switching
rule: Directive 2014/92/EU Art. 10: the receiving PSP asks the transferring PSP within 2 business days of authorisation. The transferring PSP sends lists and information within 5 business days. The receiving PSP sets up standing orders and direct debits within 5 business days of receiving them. The transferring PSP transfers the remaining balance and closes the account on the consumer's date, which must be at least 6 business days after the receiving PSP gets the documents. That gives roughly 12-13 business days end to end.
citation: Directive 2014/92/EU, Article 10
uncertainty: Low on the 2/5/5 steps. Medium on the exact anchor for the 6-day minimum and the summed total (summary-model reading).

question: 11. Kontowechselhilfe (ZKG §§ 20-26)
rule: Payment Accounts Act (Zahlungskontengesetz, in force Sept 2016): new bank asks old bank within 2 business days; old bank sends 13 months of lists within 5 business days; new bank sets up within 5 business days. Total is 12 business days.

question: 11. Mobilité bancaire (Loi Macron)
rule: Service-Public: 22 working days (jours ouvrés) from the signed mandate. Arrival bank has 2 days to request; departure bank has 5 days to send 13 months of debits and transfers; arrival bank has 5 days to notify payers and payees; those organisations have 10 days to process. Free of charge.
citation: service-public.gouv.fr F33881
uncertainty: Low
gameImplication: 22 working days.

question: 11. Switching Code
rule: Central Bank of Ireland Code of Conduct on the Switching of Payment Accounts (2016): the old bank completes its steps within 7 working days of the switch date, and the new account must be active within 10 working days of the agreed switching date. The EU PAD also applies.
citation: Central Bank of Ireland 2016 Switching Code; CCPC

question: 11. Switching
rule: No full switching service. Since 2012 (ASIC media release 12-139MR), the old institution must give the new one, on request, a list of regular direct debits and credits for the past 13 months; the customer redirects them. The Consumer Data Right (CDR) also enables data sharing.
